clue.text: One on a tour, jazz singer Billie with producer

parts.note: Billie Holiday was the American jazz singer
a maker is one who produces something

explanation.surface: A list of travellers: a tourist, the jazz singer Billie Holiday and a record producer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is a person away on a trip or excursion for pleasure, which is what someone on a tour is.

clue.text: Leading chapter includes island matter

indicators.note: includes means the first pieces take the next one within them

parts.note: leading means at the top

explanation.surface: A book's opening chapter takes in an island as its subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter under discussion is a subject or theme; the two words are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: Welcoming drink

definitions.meaning: warm and friendly in manner, as a host greeting guests
a sweet fruit-flavoured concentrate diluted to drink, or a liqueur

explanation.surface: A friendly drink offered to arriving guests.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for warm friendliness and a noun for a sweet diluted or alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Regrets present undone

indicators.note: something undone has come apart, so these letters are taken apart and remade

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry that a gift arrived unwrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel remorse or sorrow over something done is to regret it; synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: It holds writer back, being cack-handed

indicators.note: holds means the first word contains the second piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back means the word for writer is read the other way round

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: A clumsy writer, perhaps, is held back by being cack-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: Cack-handed is British slang for clumsy; 'back' and 'holds' are the signals, and 'It' is used as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Cack-handed is British slang for clumsy or lacking skill, the same idea as incompetent.

clue.text: Pull in small coach

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: An athlete picks up a muscle pull during a short training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull' can be read as a tug, but it is a muscle injury here.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulled muscle is one overstretched or injured, which is a synonym in the sporting injury sense.

clue.text: Understand about daughter getting to be furious

parts.note: to see is to understand, as in 'I see'
re is Latin for 'about', concerning

explanation.surface: A parent grasps what a daughter is doing and becomes livid.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for becoming suddenly very angry, as a bull is said to react to a red cape.

clue.text: Breed fish, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for fish is said, not written, to give the answer

parts.note: rays are flat cartilaginous fish such as skates

explanation.surface: An instruction to a fish farmer to breed fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear or bring up animals is to breed them; the two verbs are synonyms in farming.

clue.text: Stage attraction's good-humoured hoax

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
pull means attraction or draw; the 's stands for 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A theatrical draw turns out to be a friendly prank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' suggests the theatre, but it means a leg of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling someone's leg means teasing them, so the noun is a playful joke or deception.

clue.text: Petty quarrel with a New York jeweller

parts.note: a tiff is a minor squabble

explanation.surface: A New York jeweller gets into a minor squabble.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffany & Co. is the famous jewellery firm founded in New York, so this is an example.

clue.text: A young lady, out of order

parts.note: Miss is the title for a young or unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A girl is said to be behaving badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrong, faulty or not as it should be: out of order and this word are synonyms.

clue.text: Hard bargaining at the Newmarket sales?

definitions.text: Hard bargaining at the Newmarket sales?

parts.words: Hard bargaining at the Newmarket sales?
parts.note: Newmarket in Suffolk is the home of British horse racing and its bloodstock auctions, so the tough haggling there is literally over horses

explanation.surface: Tough haggling at the famous racehorse auctions in Newmarket.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket is an English town famous for racing and racehorse sales; the idiom for shrewd negotiation is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means shrewd, hard-nosed negotiation, originally the haggling of dealers in livestock.

clue.text: Working daily? In theory

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
a daily is a newspaper published every day

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person works every day, and answers that it is so in principle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true in writing or by calculation but perhaps not in practice is true theoretically.

clue.text: Uncaring behind bars, prisoner being held on charge

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first part sits above the next
being held means the prisoner is enclosed within the word for behind bars

parts.note: inside is slang for in prison
a con is a convict
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A prison scene: a callous inmate held on a criminal charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being held' is the containment signal and 'on' stacks the parts in this down clue. 'charge' looks like a criminal charge but is a price.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoughtless of others' feelings is the same as uncaring; the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Point the finger at copper in corrupt case

indicators.note: in means the symbol for copper goes inside the other letters
corrupt means the letters of case are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Blaming a police officer for a corrupt court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman but is the metal; 'corrupt' scrambles and 'in' places the metal's symbol within.
explanation.definitionFit: To point the finger at someone is an idiom for blaming or charging them.

clue.text: German elder in new German opera

indicators.note: new means the letters are formed into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An older German man appears in a new German opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' at the end is the English composer Edward German, not the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Merrie England is a 1902 comic opera by the English composer Edward German, so this is an example of his work.

clue.text: Fluid upset over iron blade

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above the next
in a down clue, upset means the word for fluid is turned upside down

parts.note: ink is a fluid for writing
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Liquid is spilt on an iron blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns INK into KNI, and 'over' sets it above FE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting tool consisting of a sharp edge set in a handle; a blade is the cutting part, used for the whole.

clue.text: Told of the same family

definitions.meaning: past tense of 'relate', to tell or narrate

explanation.surface: Someone was informed that people share a family.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word is the past tense of the verb meaning narrate, and an adjective meaning kin.

clue.text: Celebrity beginning to lose tail

indicators.note: lose tail means the last letter of the word for beginning is dropped

parts.note: a start is a beginning

explanation.surface: A famous person at the start of a career fades from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous performer or personality is called a celebrity; the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Withdraw with slight injury

definitions.meaning: to pull out of a race or contest before it starts
a minor graze or cut on the skin

explanation.surface: An athlete pulls out of an event because of a minor hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means pulling out a competitor before the start; the noun is a shallow mark on the skin.

clue.text: Meeting of old pals, sappers, prior to wedding

indicators.note: prior to means the first piece comes before the next

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps whose soldiers are called sappers
a union is a marriage

explanation.surface: Army comrades get together before one of them marries.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are military engineers; in Britain they belong to the Royal Engineers, abbreviated RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of people who were once together, such as former classmates, is a reunion.

clue.text: Power: film actor

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
a film is a thin layer, as of dust

explanation.surface: A film actor wields power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' suggests the cinema but is a thin coating.
explanation.definitionFit: One who plays a part on stage or screen is a performer, a synonym for actor.

clue.text: Gather popular judge is to come over

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: to come over means the word for judge is turned round, read upwards in a down clue

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, judges a match

explanation.surface: We gather that a well-liked judge is coming to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come over' turns REF into FER.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather a conclusion is to deduce it from evidence; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Survive violent verbal outpouring? Not bishop

indicators.note: Not means the letter for bishop is left out of the word for the outpouring

parts.note: a blast is a fierce verbal attack, a rant
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Endure a tirade, though not one delivered by a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going or endure over time is to survive; synonyms as verbs.
